name: South Dakota
tagline: From Black Hills granite tunnels and Badlands overlooks to the dams of the Missouri.
intro: South Dakota's byways thread the granite spires and limestone canyons of the Black Hills and run the Badlands rim, then follow the Missouri River north through the lands of the Sioux tribes. This chapter follows the South Dakota Scenic Byways Program, run by the South Dakota Department of Transportation, with designations made by the South Dakota Transportation Commission. The state says it has six State Scenic Byways but publishes no list, so the chapter gives the five it and Travel South Dakota identify; three of them also carry national or national forest designation.

members.name: Badlands Loop State Scenic Byway
members.blurb: SD 240 crosses Badlands National Park for 39 miles between Cactus Flat and Wall, with a dozen roadside overlooks along the way, the Ben Reifel Visitor Center at Cedar Pass and a gravel spur out along Sage Creek Rim.

members.name: Native American National and State Scenic Byway
members.blurb: The Missouri River leads this road from the Chief Standing Bear Bridge to Kenel across the lands of five Sioux tribes, past the Big Bend and Oahe dams and the granite bust of Sitting Bull at Mobridge.

members.name: Peter Norbeck National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: About 70 miles of Black Hills road joining the Needles Highway and Iron Mountain Road, through granite tunnels as narrow as eight feet and around wooden pigtail bridges, with Mount Rushmore framed in the tunnel mouths.

members.name: Spearfish Canyon State and National Forest Service Scenic Byway
members.blurb: US 14A follows Spearfish Creek for 19 miles between limestone walls from Cheyenne Crossing to Spearfish, on a rail grade abandoned after the 1933 flood, past Roughlock and Bridal Veil falls and the old stop at Savoy.

members.name: Wildlife Loop State Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Eighteen miles of park road through prairie and ponderosa hills in Custer State Park, where some 1,350 bison roam free and a band of feral burros near the southeast bend begs from passing cars.
